answer.rationale: With the contract expiring in 14 days and the assembly line running at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, any supplier transition (switch_primary_vendor) carries unacceptable delivery risk in the available window; onboarding a new vendor or even a second source under this timeline could interrupt scheduled deliveries. Negotiate_terms is already foreclosed this cycle since the incumbent explicitly refused to reopen price. Defer_decision is not viable given the hard 14-day, non-auto-renewing expiration. That leaves renew_incumbent as the only path that avoids increasing delivery risk, consistent with memory_c1's record of stable integration and uninterrupted deliveries across renewal cycles — verified here because its stability claim is load-context dependent and needs confirming it holds at high utilization with no buffer. This does not satisfy the 18% cost-cut mandate, so that downstream cost/value risk is explicitly flagged for the next review cycle, where negotiate_terms or add_second_source can be pursued once capacity or timeline pressure eases.
